sequence.timestamp_policy: 30 fps assumed; timestamps synthesized as local frame index * 1000/30 ms because images carry no timestamps

model.name: onnx-runtime-detector
model.produces: untrusted RawDetection records in processed-image pixels
model.timing_scope: detector call wall time: preprocessing + session.run + decode/NMS/coordinate inversion; not pure ONNX inference time
notes: The model artifact is a local, Git-ignored deployment file.
trained_accuracy_reported is null: repository metrics are not reproduced at load time.
Predictions are visual estimates and are validated downstream.
The detector is not connected to the connectome or plasticity.

rules.negative_coordinates: rejected when the overflow exceeds the tolerance

boundary_policy.justification: Letterbox inversion and floating-point rounding can place a true edge a fraction of a pixel outside the processed image. A 1 px tolerance absorbs that numerical artifact while any larger overflow still fails closed. Both boxes are retained so clipping is auditable rather than silent.

reproducibility.note: Both runs created a new ONNX session, perception pipeline, tracker, temporal encoder, scheduler and simulator from the same inputs, configuration and seed.

limitations: This is an engineering integration experiment, not evidence of gameplay success or biological perception.
Frames carry no source timestamps; 30 fps is assumed and timestamps are synthesized as (local_index) * 1000/30 ms.
The detector was trained on the same recording groups; the sequence is held out by recording in the fixed split and LOGO fold 1, but there is no independent test set.
No annotated object identities exist, so tracker-ID switches cannot be distinguished from real object changes. Reported track ids are tracker ids, not object identities.
The v15 schema has no player and no coin class. Player movement, jumping, rolling and coin observations are therefore unavailable, not inferred.
Lane, distance and velocity are image geometry. Distance is an uncalibrated bottom-edge proxy, not metres.
Occlusion is inferred from missed associations, not observed directly.
Spikes are model output under configured assumptions, not measured biological activity. The connectome is fixed and no plasticity is used.
No action is selected anywhere in this chain.
action_selection: none; the chain ends at sensory current injection
